Round 2 tuning+correctness. MEASURED the cost curve (new scripts/costcurve.mjs -> progress/cost-curve.md): near the floor frame_ms ~ 20.8 + 838*MP on this SwiftShader box, so ~21ms is resolution-independent and no render scale can remove it. FIXED: (1) buildScene built the world BEFORE applyRung, so character-anatomy always used rung 15's LOD mix on every device - base scene 137,760 tris/69 dc -> 52,044/27, rung 0 now 48,340 tris/21 dc, inside the floor tier's 90k cap; (2) added the missing consumer of the EXPENSIVE rung queue - actors are rebuilt at the play boundary, never on the frame path; (3) rung 0 re-cut 0.50 -> 0.11 render scale and rung 2 0.60 -> 0.50 (it exceeded the floor tier's own 0.50 cap), chosen from real harness runs via new --rung-scale; (4) heap 'sawtooth' was Math.max(saw, peak-trough) conflating GC amplitude with total run excursion, plus boot garbage collected inside the measured window - perf.mjs now forces a GC at warmup end and reports amplitude and range separately: 24.84MB -> 0.61MB; the one 157-492ms longtask was that same boot GC and is now gone; (5) gpuProbe used gl.finish() which does not sync Chrome's command buffer - it reported ms:0 for all four points while burning 1.2s of boot, so classify() silently skipped the whole GPU branch; now uses readPixels; (6) scaler windows were frame-counted so descent was SLOWEST when the device was worst (30 frames = 3.5s at 116ms/frame) - added time-bounded early close and a multi-rung panic drop, both DOWN-only so 8:2 hysteresis is intact. PROVEN: pinned 30 at rung 0, 0 drops in 602 frames, 0 bad 3s windows, worst 33.5ms. simtest 66/66. Capture stills byte-identical (md5 20aa3a40 pre and post).

text: Instrumented rather than reasoned. The blocked front three tripped the pressure threshold at tick 66, the passer got a free early throw at 73, and the ball was gone before anyone arrived — the EXTRA blitzers were saving him. Pocket rebuilt on a three-blocker cap: surplus rushers run free, spare blockers double rather than idle, a block sells time then loses, blitzers walk up, and a flush is a decision to throw only if there is somewhere to go. Sack rate monotone: 6r 41% / 4r 28% / 3r 12% / 2r 0%.

gap: The rush is fixed but nothing proves the assertions can fail. Built a mutation battery of 16 real defects: 13 killed, 3 SURVIVED. 32 real clubs, real colours, crests, division rail. The screen is FAITHFUL -- the defect it surfaces is upstream in the roster data: Chicago's featured star is Night Train Lane at ovr 98, the highest-rated Bear, and he never played for the Bears. He played for the Chicago CARDINALS, whose lineage the same workbook separately records under ARI as 'Chicago/St. Louis/Arizona Cardinals'. The ingest is faithful to a source the user designated, so it is reported rather than overruled. The other 20 cross-club duplicates are legitimate (Brady NE/TB, Moss NE/MIN, Woodson BAL/PIT).

THE BALL HAS BEEN A FLAT DISC IN EVERY CAPTURE THIS PROJECT HAS EVER TAKEN, and it was adapt.js, not the ball geometry -- which is a correct prolate lathe with pointed ends and laces. rotQ was hard-coded to identity, pinning the football's long axis across the field, so any pass thrown downfield was viewed exactly end-on. I had misattributed it to impact-fx twice. Fixed: the nose follows the flight tangent including the arc, spiralling about its long axis; 105 in-flight samples, all unit quaternions, nose on the line in every one.

The three ids the builder shipped without ever seeing rendered -- dive_catch, airborne_hit, blown_back -- are now captured and judged. dive_catch reads: fully horizontal, real extension, a clean line. blown_back reads: tumbling head-low, which is the right violence for this game. The weak one is the arms-overhead airborne pose -- both arms perfectly vertical and parallel with the legs together, which is stiff where every other pose in this piece has asymmetry. And a structural note on the scene rather than the poses: airborne_hit and blown_back are REACTION poses, and an iso scene with no ball and no contact partner cannot show what they are reacting to. They need to be staged against the tackler that caused them, the way iso_pose_truck stages its pair.

The spring's output is never validated against anything: every guard runs on the IDEAL camera and the frame renders from body.p, which no guard sees. 4692 live frames swept -- camera BELOW THE TURF on 7.4% (min -1.122 m), ball outside the safe rect on 14.0% (max ndc 2.49) on a piece whose own header calls that 'THE ONE RULE THAT OUTRANKS EVERY OTHER RULE'. Confirmed by capture at seed 5 t=1.65: no field in frame, players floating feet-first in the sky.

The hero frame is a firework, not a collision. Debris is 3x too big and 7x too tightly clustered -- 13% of frame width against the bar's 93% -- so the element panel-leveler leans on hardest vanishes and the sparks, 17:1 brighter, own the frame. Also: the ball's laces and stripes are invisible (interior sd 3%, ZERO stripe pixels) because emissive is 3x albedo; and the 0.62 profile exponent cannot produce a pointed tip for any p<1.

text: All three proven defects closed. Camera below turf 7.4% -> 0.00% (min +0.689 m); ball outside safe rect 14.0% -> 0.085%. Horizon re-solved from a re-measurement of the bar panels (they read 60-76%, not the 40-62% the code claimed) via the identity horizonFrac = topAt + fill*(1-height/1.75); delivered 32/39/22/49% -> 64/66/53/64%, confirmed IN PIXELS at 68% on a fresh capture.
